The Vikings' backfield for Sunday's game against the Lions will be co-led by Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason, but the elevation of Dallas indicates that rookie sixth-rounder Demond Claiborne could be a healthy scratch for Week 8. Dallas played 19 snaps (six on offense, 13 on special teams) in Week 7 against the Colts but didn't show up on the box score otherwise.

On a day where Minnesota held Indianapolis' offense almost completely in check, Cashman arguably shined brighter than any other player on his unit. It was the first time he's ever logged two sacks in a single game, and his four pass breakups marked another career high. He profiles as a strong IDP option in most formats going into a Week 8 matchup at Detroit.

Smith sealed Minnesota's victory in Week 7 when he cut off a Daniel Jones pass intended for tight end Will Mallory with less than two minutes remaining in regulation. It was his first interception of the season, and the 40th of his illustrious career with the Vikings. He projects to play a rotational role again in Week 8 at Detroit.

Reichard was unable to remain perfect Sunday, but he did deliver at least three field goals for the fifth straight game. The kicker converted kicks from 28 and 47 yards in the first half before later adding a 52-yard make with 1:39 left in regulation, giving Minnesota a 16-10 lead. Reichard's first miss of the season came in the fourth quarter when Grover Stewart got a paw on the kicker's 59-yard try. Reichard is out to a remarkable start to the season, going 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, over six contests so far.

Price was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion, but he's been cleared to return to Sunday's contest. He'll see most of his playing time as a returner on special teams while operating in a rotational role on offense.

Darrisaw has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The starting left tackle will protect Kyler Murray as the Vikings attempt to maintain a perfect record through Week 7.

Hollins last saw game action in Week 4, but it's possible that his absence could be capped at the minimum mandated four contests. Prior to sustaining his calf injury, Hollins had recorded a 15/209/0 receiving line on 20 targets, and if he's able to return to action Sunday against the Packers, a key role in the offense could await, with A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) Week 9 status cloudy.

Brown was inactive for Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins, and Vrabel's comment Monday implies that the wideout's status for this weekend's game against the Packers is uncertain at this stage. In Brown's absence versus Miami, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams paced the Patriots' Week 8 WR corps.

Williams made the most of his only touch in Week 8, scoring on a 43-yard deep ball from Drake Maye in the third quarter. The wide receiver had an opportunity to be more involved with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined Sunday, but Williams saw just one target for the third game in a row. On the year, the wide receiver has now caught seven of 13 targets for 190 yards and two touchdowns over eight regular-season contests.

Most of his production came on a nifty 48-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter, as Douglas took a strike from Drake Maye along the sideline but then curled back toward the middle of the field and dashed the remaining 30 yards to the end zone while out-racing four Miami defenders. It was the fourth touchdown of the season for the fourth-year wideout, a new career high, and Douglas will take a 26-332-4 line on 37 targets through eight games into a Week 9 tilt against the Packers.

With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) unavailable, Stevenson led the Patriots in rushing yards and scrimmage yards, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone. His 19 totes and 82 rushing yards were both season highs. The veteran back's workload in Week 9 against the Packers will depend somewhat on Henderson's health, but Stevenson appears to be Mike Vrabel's most trusted option in the backfield, and through eight games he's on pace to top 1,000 scrimmage yards for the first time since 2022.

While he failed to reach 200 passing yards for the third time in eight games this season, Maye put together a very efficient performance as he produced multiple TDs for a fifth straight game. All three scores came in the second half as the QB rallied the Patriots from a 13-3 deficit, hitting Kyle Williams for a 43-yard score in the third quarter and DeMario Douglas for a 48-yard strike in the fourth, while running for a two-yard TD in between. Maye appears to have gotten his recklessness under control, committing just one turnover in the last four contests, and he'll take a 15:8 TD:INT on the season into a Week 9 clash with the Packers.

Henry exited in the first half of this Week 8 matchup and eventually was ruled out midway through the fourth quarter. He ended with three catches (on three targets) for 30 yards. Eli Raridon will act as the Patriots' top pass-catching tight end for as long as Henry is sidelined.

Jacas suffered a knee injury in the second half and he may now be forced to miss the final stretch of the game. In his absence, Elijah Ponder and Dre'Mont Jones will operate as the team's two primary options at outside linebacker versus the Dolphins.
As the emergency third quarterback, Morton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Elliss has been cleared to play Sunday after working through a chest injury during Week 8 prep. He has 51 tackles (29 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through seven regular-season games.

Davis has been cleared to return form a three-game absence due to a neck injury he picked up in Week 4 against the Bills. He'll resume his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez while Charles Woods provides depth at the position.

Bryant initially drew the questionable tag after logging full practices Thursday and Friday, but he's not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve. His next chance to play is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

The Patriots needed more depth at wide receiver after the team ruled out A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Miller played in each of the Dolphins' first five games of the regular season before being cut by the team Oct. 13. He could see some snaps on offense while working as the WR4 behind DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams.

The addition of Larison to the 53-man roster gives the Patriots more depth in the backfield, and he could see some offensive snaps against the Dolphins on Sunday due to the absence of TreVeyon Henderson (illness). Larison figures to operate as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner.

Brown was unable play against the Bears in Week 7 due to a knee injury. He's faded an injury tag for Sunday's game after logging a full practice Friday, and he should reclaim his starting spot at right guard.

Jones finished second on New England in stops behind Christian Elliss (13). He also notched his first sack of the campaign, bringing down Caleb Williams on a second-down play near the end of the first half, though Chicago scored a touchdown on its following snap. Jones is off to a strong start to the campaign, recording 36 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) and five defensed passes (including an interception) through seven contests.

Kiner came into Thursday having gained 50-plus rushing yards in consecutive contests, but he was much less impactful versus the Bears. Part of that was due to New England playing from behind and tallying just 17 total carries as a team (to 31 pass attempts), but it's also notable that Kiner logged just six offensive snaps, well behind Rhamondre Stevenson's 37 and less than half of TreyVeon Henderson's 13. While Kiner's previous two performances gave him a little momentum in fantasy, he's unlikely to be a reliable asset while Stevenson and Henderson are healthy.

Raridon got open late in the third quarter and hauled in a nicely placed pass from Drake Maye for a 30-yard score. The rookie tight end finished third on the team with 56 receiving yards and tied for third with three receptions. Raridon is clearly behind Hunter Henry, who posted a 7-71-0 receiving line on seven targets, in the tight-end pecking order, but he's shown promise early in his career with 12 catches on 16 targets for 168 yards and two TDs through six games.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reported over the weekend that Tyson could have a chance at making his NFL debut as soon as this coming Sunday against the Browns, but until the Saints formally clear the wideout to practice, a target date for him to play will remain somewhat muddled.

Granderson helped keep the game close with a pair of key sacks. He brought down Aaron Rodgers near the end of the second quarter to help hold the Steelers to a field goal, then split a sack in the red zone at the end of the third period to again limit Pittsburgh to three points. Granderson is up to 5.5 sacks through six games on the campaign, giving him an excellent chance of surpassing the career-high mark of 8.5 sacks he established over 17 contests in 2023.

Werner had a two-game streak of double-digit stops snapped, but he was still plenty productive. The veteran linebacker dealt with a neck injury in early October but appears past that issue, as he's played every Saints defensive snap in three straight contests. Werner leads New Orleans with 54 tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through seven games.

Sanker recorded his second-highest tackle tally of the campaign to lead New Orleans in that category. The second-year defender has now tallied six or more stops in five of his seven games this season. With 44 tackles through seven contests, Sanker is easily on pace to surpass the 80 stops he notched in 17 games as a rookie.

After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.

The Saints got absolutely nothing going on the ground against Pittsburgh, rushing 17 times for 18 yards as a team, so it's not like Miller and his team-leading eight carries was the only issue. New Orleans heads into its bye in Week 8, and Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off injured reserve for Week 9 against the Browns. When both Etienne and Alvin Kamara were healthy and active together earlier this season, Miller was a healthy inactive.

Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass catcher moving forward.

Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

The third-year wideout was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD pass of the day, hauling in a one-yard toss in the second quarter for the Saints' final points. Vele tied his career high with his third touchdown of the season, and his 33-348-3 line on 48 targets through seven games has him tracking toward a career-best campaign heading into a Week 8 bye. His role could shrink significantly after the bye, however, if rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to make his NFL debut.

The Saints' ground game was completely shut down, as quarterback Tyler Shough led the team with a mere seven rushing yards, but Kamara still contributed through the air and led New Orleans in catches while tying Barion Brown for the game high in receiving yards. Since missing the season opener, Kamara has put together 258 scrimmage yards and three total TDs (two rushing, one receiving) over six games, but the backfield could get more crowded after a Week 8 bye if Travis Etienne (hamstring) is cleared to return.

Carlson connected on a 38-yard field goal early in the second quarter, but his 52-yarder in the fourth missed wide right and gave the Steelers the ball back with good field position. He's missed one kick in each of his last five games, and head coach Kellen Moore told reporters after Sunday's contest that "it's fair to evaluate" Carlson's kicking issues to open the season, per Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com. The Saints will be on a bye for Week 8, so the team could bring in another kicker to compete with Carlson before their next game in Week 9 against the Browns on Sunday, Nov. 8.

With the Saints' ground game getting absolutely nowhere -- Shough actually led the team in rushing yards -- the second-year QB had to air it out frequently once again, but the volume didn't result in much production. Shough will head into a Week 8 bye averaging 39 pass attempts a game -- the fourth-highest mark in the league behind Matthew Stafford, Dak Prescott and Bryce Young -- to go along with a 13:6 TD:INT and 1,721 passing yards.

While Olave saw a team-high 10 targets, Alvin Kamara caught one more pass and gained one more receiving yard for the team leads in those categories, while Devaughn Vele caught Tyler Shough's only TD. Olave has failed to reach 60 yards in three straight games after topping 100 in three of his first four contests this season, but he'll get a bye week to reset before facing the Browns in Week 9.

Reid sustained a concussion in Sunday's international game and will not return to the contest. The safety has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist for every step of his return journey.

Donaldson picked up the injury during the first quarter and has been taken to the locker room to undergo more tests on his shoulder injury. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller would be the remaining healthy running backs on the Saints active roster for the rest of Sunday's game if Donaldson is not cleared to return.

Rattler was able to beat out Zach Wilson for the top backup job behind Tyler Shough during the preseason and has maintained his positioning on the depth chart all season. For the seventh week in a row, Wilson will be inactive as the Saints' emergency No. 3 signal-caller.

Jennings will play in his first contest since sustaining a knee injury in the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. The linebacker should work back into the edge rotation behind starters Chase Young and Carl Granderson.

The Giants have their bye in Week 8, but Tracy will be required to miss at least four games with his injury, so it appears Singletary and Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will form the backfield duo with Tracy sidelined and Najee Harris recently released. Singletary scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime last Sunday against the Texans, finishing with 55 total yards and the touchdown on eight touches. If Skattebo is healthy, he figures to operate as the lead back, but Singletary showed enough to warrant 6-to-10 touches with upside for more. He's worth picking up in most fantasy leagues.

Reese continues to produce nice tackle numbers, as he's recorded seven or more stops in five of his seven games this season. The rookie out of Ohio State didn't notch a sack in his first four contests, but he's starting to pick up the pace with 1.5 sacks across his past three games. Reese has logged 100 percent of New York's defensive snaps in all but one of his appearances so far.

Among McFadden's 10 stops were two tackles for loss. The veteran linebacker had logged only three defensive snaps while serving primarily on special teams before Sunday, but he stepped into a starting role and played every one of the Giants' defensive snaps against Houston. It appears McFadden is going to be the replacement for inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, who landed on IR due to a chest injury last week.

With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) now on injured reserve, the Giants bolstered the roster by adding Desrosiers. The undrafted rookie appeared in three preseason games for the Chargers, amassing 166 yards and one touchdown off 23 carries. While Desrosiers is listed behind Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Devin Singletary on the depth chart, he could see action if one of those players gets injured.

Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.

Mooney has now been held to one or no catches in three of the past four games, and he has yet to exceed two receptions in a contest this season. The wide receiver will continue to be an unattractive fantasy option when the Giants return to action Week 9 against the Eagles.

The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy to serve as the starting quarterback for Week 7 after Winston filled in that role in each of the four prior games. McCarthy looked more poised in the pocket, but all four of the Giants' touchdowns came on the ground, with Winston finding the end zone on a designed QB sneak late in the second quarter. That figures to be the veteran's role moving forward unless McCarthy misses time.

Though the Giants escaped with a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans on Sunday, Zvada had his second rough performance in the past three weeks. The undrafted rookie out of Michigan was unable to connect on field-goal tries of 44 and 56 yards, giving him five misses on 18 attempts through seven games. The Giants are hoping that their upcoming Week 8 bye will give Zvada some time to iron out kinks and refine his approach before the team returns to action Nov. 8 versus the Eagles.

Skattebo's explosive run put the Giants within field-goal range before he was subbed out for Devin Singletary, who ran up the middle for a 30-yard score to seal the win on the very next play. Though he told Dan Graziano of ESPN.com after the game that he "felt something" in his hamstring that prompted him to slide down at the end of his run rather than being tackled to the ground, Skattebo doesn't sound like he'll require an MRI and should be ready to play in the Giants' next game Nov. 8 versus the Eagles following a Week 8 bye. After being limited to just six snaps in a Week 6 loss to the Saints following a string of poor outings to begin the campaign, Skattebo stepped back into a lead role out of the backfield in Sunday's victory and delivered his best performance of the season, finishing with 121 total yards and a touchdown on 18 touches.

With J.J. McCarthy inserted under center for his first start with the Giants, Likely took a big hit in production, as Malik Nabers led the team in targets (nine), catches (seven) and yards (111) despite the tough on-paper matchup with cornerback Derek Stingley. Likely will try to get back on track coming out of the Week 8 bye when the Giants face the Eagles on the road in Week 9.

In J.J. McCarthy's first start of the season, Fields had his best performance as a pro, capping his day with a 47-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter. The rookie wideout set a new career high in both receiving yards and catches after hauling in exactly two passes in each of his first six games for the Giants. Fields will head into the Giants' bye with a 16-248-1 line on 30 targets before facing the Eagles in Week 9.

Making his first start of the season, McCarthy was efficient in getting the Giants into position to score, but all four of their touchdowns came on the ground -- including a one-yard plunge by the man he replaced under center, Jameis Winston, in the second quarter. The victory alone was enough to keep McCarthy in the starting job, and after a bye he'll gear up for a Week 9 clash with the Eagles.

The switch from Jameis Winston to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback for the Giants hasn't slowed Nabers down at all, and the team's No. 1 wideout extended his streak of games with over 100 receiving yards to four. During that surge, Nabers has delivered a 36-509-2 line on 51 targets, as he puts his injury-marred sophomore NFL campaign firmly behind him. He'll try to not to lose his momentum during the bye before facing the Eagles in Week 9.

Eluemunor managed just a pair of limited practices this week, but the veteran tackle will ultimately be available for a Giants team that has both Marcus Mbow (knee) and Josh Sills (coach's decision) on the inactive list Sunday.

After missing Week 6, Nubin will retake the field against Houston following a week of limited practices. Presumably in line to start, Nubin has recorded three or more combined tackles in each of the four games he has appeared in this year.

Adebo was activated from IR this week but still had a questionable tag after a week of limited practices. He'll ultimately get the nod to play for the first time since Week 1, and the veteran corner stands to see a significant number of snaps due to Greg Newsome (concussion) getting ruled out, plus several other members of the New York secondary are on IR.

Edmunds will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn chest muscle, so his placement on injured reserve opens up a spot on the Giants' 53-man roster. Micah McFadden is expected to start at inside linebacker alongside Arvell Reese for the rest of the season in Edmunds' absence, with Jack Kelly and Zaire Barnes providing depth at the position.

Thomas ended Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He's been working through a groin injury the last few weeks but hasn't missed a game this season.

Though he was sidelined for a fifth straight game in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders, Hall displayed progress in his recovery from a right quad injury by practicing on a limited practice participant throughout Week 8 prep. As long as he's able to upgrade to full activity at some point during Week 9, Hall should get the green light to play in Kansas City, but he may not be guaranteed a full workload while backup Braelon Allen has likely earned himself more opportunities by averaging 114.8 scrimmage yards per game in Hall's absence over the last five contests.

Williams ran a total of one route on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks against Las Vegas, but he made it count with a red-zone touchdown. The Jets' fourth receiver behind Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, Williams has no fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's date with the Chiefs.

Cooper entered Week 8 having topped 100 receiving yards with a touchdown in back-to-back games, so Sunday's performance was especially disappointing. The rookie wideout was overshadowed by Adonai Mitchell (7-142-1) and Garrett Wilson (6-83-0) in the game, and it'll be hard to predict his workload ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Chiefs.

Smith threw second-quarter touchdown passes of 18 yards to Isaiah Williams and 12 yards to Adonai Mitchell while coming 10 yards shy of his second 300-yard passing performance of the season. The veteran QB had a chance to orchestrate a game-winning drive against his former team, but the Jets' comeback bid came up short when Smith threw an end-zone interception from the Raiders' 35-yard line with seven seconds remaining. Smith has been picked off in each of his last three outings after going without an interception through five starts to open his second tenure with the Jets. He'll take a 12:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 trip to Kansas City.

Mitchell didn't catch any of his three targets in the Week 7 loss to Miami after returning from a four-game absence due to a finger injury, but he bounced back with a career-best Week 8 performance. His top highlights Sunday were a 12-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter and a 47-yard reception in the fourth quarter. Garrett Wilson led the team with 12 targets while Omar Cooper went without a target after back-to-back games with more than 100 yards and a TD. The 2-6 Jets could try to get all three of their talented young wideouts involved in Week 9, when they will likely be playing catch-up against the Chiefs.

Wilson saw his second-highest target total of the season Sunday after being targeted a season-low three times in the Week 7 loss to Miami. After being outplayed by Omar Cooper in each of the previous two games, Wilson took a back seat to Adonai Mitchell in this one, as Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown while Cooper went without a target. The Jets have three capable wide receivers for the first time in a while, but Wilson easily leads the team with 527 receiving yards heading into a Week 9 road game against the Chiefs, while Mitchell's a distant second with 265 receiving yards.

Allen made a fifth consecutive start in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps) and exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fourth consecutive game. The 2024 fourth-round pick set a new career high with 147 rushing yards, surpassing Allen's 116 yards on the ground in the Week 5 win over the Browns. Allen scored his third rushing touchdown of the season on a 21-yard run in the third quarter to give the Jets a 30-21 lead, but the Raiders closed the game on a 17-3 run to drop the Jets to 2-6. If Hall's ready to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs, the Jets could opt for a backfield split between Allen and Hall.

Parham will be back in action for the first time since Week 3, when he sustained a knee injury in a loss to the Lions. Though he was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, Parham was cleared to play after logging a pair of limited practices and a full session during the week. He should step back in as the Jets' starting left guard, sending Jordan Meredith back to the bench.

Bailey suffered a groin injury during the Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. He didn't practice throughout the week and will now miss his first game of the 2026 campaign. Without Bailey on the field versus the Raiders, Nate Lynn and Will McDonald are candidates for more snaps.

Patrick spent the first four regular-season games on injured reserve. He appeared in the Jets' last three contests, though he will be a healthy scratch for the Week 8 meeting with Las Vegas. The 32-year-old has only three catches during the 2026 campaign, so his absence won't open up extra targets for others.

Sweat was diagnosed with a knee injury during the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was week-to-week, and the Jets medical staff has determined that a stint on IR is warranted for the third-year defensive lineman, although he's expected to return this season. Sweat will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29, although he could be held out until after the Jets' Week 13 bye. Darrell Jackson and Harrison Phillips will both step into more prominent roles on the defensive line in Sweat's absence.

Nwangwu remained inactive for the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins despite logging a full practice Friday. The running back has returned to form for Week 8 prep and should be all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

Davis' tackle tally was his lowest of the campaign, but he did record his first effort of multiple defensed passes. The durable linebacker has played every defensive snap for the Jets so far this season. With 46 stops through seven games, Davis is on pace for a 10th consecutive 100-tackle campaign.

Of Sherwood's eight stops, two went for a loss. He also notched multiple defensed passes for the first time this season. Sherwood has been quite disruptive so far in 2026, tallying 54 tackles, four defensed passes, two forced fumbles and a recovered fumble through seven games.

Belton continues to put together a productive season, as he's posted seven or more stops in each of his past five games. The former New York Giant has yet to miss a defensive snap this season in his first campaign as a Jet. After posting a career-high 120 stops across 17 regular-season contests last year, Belton is on pace to challenge that mark with 56 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) through seven games this year. He's also tallied three defensed passes.

Fitzpatrick's 10 stops led New York and marked his second double-digit tackle effort of the campaign. After missing Weeks 2 and 3 due to a groin injury, Fitzpatrick has logged every Jets defensive snap in four straight games as a stalwart of the team's secondary. The veteran safety has tallied 36 tackles and two defensed passes, including one interception, through five games during his first season with New York.

Davis was on the field for 25 snaps (13 on offense, 12 on special teams) during Sunday's loss. He was barely used offensively until late in the fourth quarter, when he rattled off catches of two, 41 and six yards on consecutive plays, with the drive ending on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Geno Smith to Mason Taylor. Davis has operated as the Jets' RB2 behind Braelon Allen for the Jets' last four games, but the former's role will shrink considerably if Breece Hall (quadriceps) is cleared to return for Week 8 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 1.

With Mason Taylor dominating the targets at tight end for the Jets, Sadiq continues to fade into the background for an offense that is unable to support more than a couple pass catchers in the box score each week. Sadiq has just four catches for 21 yards over the last three weeks with Taylor back in the lineup.

Sanders hit the right upright on his first field-goal attempt of the day in the third quarter, missing his first kick since Week 1. The kicker later added a 33-yard make in the fourth quarter, but his earlier miss would prove to be the difference in the loss. Sanders has now gone 13-for-15 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, over the first seven games of the 2026 season.

After dropping their sixth straight game Sunday, the Eagles now sit at 2-6 on the season and could be motivated to explore moving veteran players for draft capital ahead of the deadline. Barkley -- who is under contract through 2028 -- apparently won't be among the pieces the Eagles consider moving, as the team is counting on re-emerging as a playoff contender next season rather than embracing a long-term rebuilding effort. Though he'll be suiting up for a Week 9 matchup with the division-leading Giants, Barkley could continue to have his playing time managed while he gets ramped back up from hamstring and back injuries. He played just 22 of the Eagles' 68 offensive snaps in the loss to Washington, finishing with 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown and a 24-yard reception on his lone target.

Mitchell led the team in rushing yards while notching two fewer carries than Saquon Barkley, who was in and out of the game while playing through a back injury. Jaydon Blue, whom the Eagles signed from their practice squad Wednesday, contributed primarily as a special-teams kickoff returner while notching one catch and no carries. Mitchell has been elevated from the practice squad for each of Philadelphia's last two games, so he'll be eligible for one more elevation in Week 9 against the Giants before the Eagles have to sign him to the active roster to keep using him on game days.

McKee operated without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for a second consecutive game and failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time in his three-game stint as Philadelphia's starting QB. He has thrown for between 211 and 215 yards in each of his three outings since Jalen Hurts (calf) was shut down for the season. Expectations should remain tempered for McKee and Philadelphia's injury-riddled offense in Week 9 against the Giants.

Lemon has stepped up as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 receiver in the ongoing absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). After setting career highs across the board with seven catches for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown on eight targets in Week 7 against the Cowboys, Lemon led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets Sunday night. The rookie 20th overall pick is building momentum ahead of a Week 9 home game against the Giants, but his target share would likely drop if Smith gains clearance to return.

Goedert has 15 catches for 139 receiving yards in three games since Tanner McKee took over as Philadelphia's starting QB, but the veteran TE has now gone five consecutive appearances without a TD after scoring 13 times in the span of 15 regular-season appearances through Week 1 of this season. Goedert had a ball bounce off his hands for an interception in the second half, but the play was negated by a defensive penalty, removing what would have been the lone blemish on Goedert's otherwise clean, though unimpressive, stat sheet. He'll try to snap his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Giants.

Carter entered Week 8 questionable to play after missing the team's last two contests with an injured abdomen, and it's possible that he tweaked the injury during Sunday Night Football. In his absence, Kenny Moore is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities at safety versus Washington.

Bennett continues to recover from a knee injury that he sustained in training camp in August. He's not quite ready to return from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 9 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Smith was a full participant in Friday's practice, and he was cleared from the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa.

Elliott hasn't missed a kick all season, but he remains stuck on five field-goal attempts for the campaign, as the Eagles aren't moving the ball consistently but have found ways to punch in touchdowns when they get in scoring range. With Philadelphia banged up on offense and in the midst of a five-game losing streak, Elliott is facing some headwinds heading into a favorable Week 8 matchup on paper against the Commanders, who are giving up 28.7 points per game.

Yet another Eagles RB landed on IR on Wednesday, with Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) joining Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot). Blue thus was called up as a reinforcement and could be in line for a decent amount of work right away with Saquon Barkley (back) dealing with another health concern. Blue hasn't played in 2026 but turned 38 carries into 129 yards and one touchdown to go with one catch (on one target) for five yards in five appearances as a rookie fifth-rounder for the Cowboys last season.

Pierce thus is joining fellow RBs Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) on IR, leaving Saquon Barkley and Jaydon Blue as the only players at the position on the Eagles' active roster. Pierce made a late exit from Monday's loss to the Cowboys, which followed Barkley's own earlier departure due to a back issue. Pierce's health concern is enough for him to miss at least four contests, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, in Arizona.

DeJean racked up seven-plus tackles for the third time this season in a Week 7 contest that saw Dallas run the ball 38 times. He's on pace for the first 100-tackle season of his career, putting him on the fringe of IDP consideration of some formats ahead of a Week 8 matchup at Washington.

Dallas' offense found a ton of success on the ground in Week 7, and its 38 rush attempts created plenty of tackling opportunities for Baun. He now has nine-plus tackles in four of his six games in 2026. He figures as a high-floor IDP option in some formats heading into a Week 8 tilt at Washington.

Pittman has missed the Steelers' last four games and is now eligible to be activated from IR at any point, but based on the receiver's comments, he doesn't appear to be trending toward a return to action following the team's Week 9 bye. The wideout noted that his left foot injury that first cropped up following the season opener was originally plantar fasciitis but has since "morphed into something else." While it's encouraging that he's at least healthy enough to start running again, Pittman didn't indicate when he might be ready to resume practicing with the team.

Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.

Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

Howard will continue to operate as the emergency QB3, which means he is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Skowronek will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a calf injury, and with the Steelers on a bye for Week 9, his next chance to play is Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15. Kaden Wetjen, Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson are in line for more snaps on offense in Skowronek's absence.

Johnson will be elevated to the active roster for a third consecutive game, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man squad in order to be eligible to play for the Steelers beyond Week 8. He did not record a target across his two prior outings.

Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.

Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

Queen had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles in addition to registering his first sack of the campaign. The 2020 first-round pick has now logged 48 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across seven games this season.

Boswell opened Sunday's contest with a 28-yard chip shot early in the first quarter before connecting on field goals from 47 and 39 yards in the second and third, respectively. It's the third time this season that he has made at least three field goals, and through seven regular-season games, he is 16-for-20 on field-goal attempts (including 4-for-6 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 13-for-13 on extra-point tries. The Steelers will return home for a Week 8, AFC North showdown against the Browns on Nov. 1.

Elliott will suit up for his first game action since Oct. 26, 2025, when he sustained a knee injury that kept him out for the remainder of that season as well as the first six games of the 2026 campaign. The 29-year-old was a full participant in practice this week, and after being activated from injured reserve Saturday, he'll likely be ready to handle a full load of snaps against New Orleans. Expect Elliott to unseat rookie Robert Spears-Jennings as one of Pittsburgh's starting safeties.

Rudolph has emerged as the Steelers' preferred backup quarterback behind starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers coming out of the preseason. Through each of Pittsburgh's first seven contests, Rudolph has suited up, while both Will Howard and Drew Allar have been inactive. Howard is the Steelers' emergency No. 3 quarterback and will be called upon to play only in the event that both Rodgers and Rudolph are forced to exit Sunday's game.

Watt was limited by a calf injury Thursday, but he's good to go for Pittsburgh's Paris game against New Orleans. Through six games this season, the 32-year-old Watt has 15 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and a pick-six interception.

Greenlaw missed Week 6 against Washington while on suspension but returned Sunday and logged a season-high 91 percent defensive snap share. The veteran linebacker tied his season high with 12 tackles, finishing one behind Fred Warner for the team lead. Greenlaw is enjoying a productive return to San Francisco with 49 tackles and a forced fumble through six contests.

Warner led the 49ers in tackles, finishing one ahead of Dre Greenlaw. It was the fourth time through seven games that Warner has notched double-digit stops. The star linebacker ranks second in the NFL with 71 tackles through seven games.

Kirk was activated off injured reserve Saturday and was cleared to make his 2026 debut following a near three-month absence due to a calf injury that he sustained during training camp in July. His 20 offensive snaps were fourth most among 49ers wide receivers, and while he was being eased back into things, his lack of targets was a bit of a let down considering the 49ers were without both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Both of San Francisco's top pass catchers could be back in action following the Week 8 bye, so Kirk's role for Week 9 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8 is uncertain.

Cooks was in line to serve as the 49ers' top wide receiver for Week 7 due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 45 offensive snaps were second-most among 49ers wideouts behind Jordan Watkins (50), although the former had only once catch to show for his extra playing time, which didn't happen until the final minute of the fourth quarter. Cooks has three catches (on seven targets) for 33 yards and a touchdown over his last three games, but his role could shrink significantly following the 49ers' Week 8 bye depending on the statuses of Evans, Samuel Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson (ankle, IR).

Cowing and the other 49ers pass catchers operated in expanded roles Sunday due to the absences of both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cowing was on the field for 26 of the 49ers' 66 offensive snaps (39.4 percent), which was third most behind Jordan Watkins (50) and Brandin Cooks (45). Cowing put up season highs in catches, receiving yards and rushing yards, but his role could shrink significantly following the 49ers' Week 8 bye depending on the statuses of Evans, Samuel, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson (ankle, IR), with rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, IR) not expected back until December, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com.

Most of James' on-field work Sunday came on special teams. Both of his touches on offense happened on back-to-back plays in the second quarter, coinciding with the absence of Christian McCaffrey, the latter of whom was playing through a thigh injury during most of Sunday's contest. The only way James would see consistent playing time on offense is if one of McCaffrey or rookie Kaelon Black were to miss time. The 49ers will get some additional rest thanks to the Week 8 bye, and their next game takes place Week 9 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout was only going to enter the game in an emergency scenario for the 49ers' secondary. The team hopes the Week 8 bye will allow Stout's shoulder sprain to fully heal ahead of the Week 9 showdown with the Raiders.

A lingering knee injury has sidelined Bosa for each of the 49ers' last five games. He has yet to return to practice, but with San Francisco getting extra rest thanks to the bye, the veteran pass rusher could be available for Week 9. Bosa's return would result in less snaps being available on the edge for the likes of Romello Height, Mykel Williams, Ogbo Okoronkwo and Khalid Kareem.

All three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Samuel and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) are eyeing a Week 9 return against the Raiders, so the 49ers' wide receiver depth chart could look vastly different coming out of the bye. Samuel would likely go back to his part-time role, handling short-area passes and an occasional handoff or two. He's not a particularly exciting fantasy play when Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) are all healthy.

Shanahan said the same thing 11 days ago, so the timeline appears to remain in place for Robinson, who suffered a high-ankle sprain way back in Week 2 against Miami. The Niners are expected to get plenty of reinforcements following their open date, and all three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Robinson could be among those returning for Week 9 against Las Vegas.

Stribling was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and remains on injured reserve. He missed a big opportunity for snaps and targets with the team dealing with so many injuries at the wide receiver position, but all indications are Stribling will be back for the stretch run and a possible trip to the playoffs.

After missing Sunday's game against the Falcons with the Achilles issue, Evans appears to be trending toward a return for San Francisco's next contest in Week 9 against the Raiders. Working as the Niners' big-play X receiver this season, Evans has been nearly unstoppable when healthy. Maintaining health has been his biggest issue. When on the field, Evans is a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside.

After McCaffrey briefly exited Sunday's loss to Atlanta with what had been described as a thigh issue, this update offers more clarity on the injury and a favorable outlook. The timing of the 49ers' bye gives the veteran running back added recovery time ahead of their next game in Week 9 versus the Raiders, though his practice status will still be worth monitoring once San Francisco returns to work. Kaelon Black will be a priority add off waivers considering CMC's injury history.

Purdy put together an impressive passing yardage total, especially considering he was down both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), along with De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle). He also lost Christian McCaffrey for the entirety of the second quarter due to a leg injury that the star back eventually returned from, but the scarcity of his top pass catchers eventually led to a more mistake-filled performance than usual. The multi-interception tally was Purdy's first of the season, and the two picks led to 10 points for the Falcons. Purdy should have a chance to work with a deeper pass-catching corps in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, as the Week 8 bye should offer multiple receivers a chance to recover from their respective injuries.

Juszczyk garnered multiple targets for the fifth straight game that he's played in, and he was able to reach paydirt for the second time this season, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the fourth quarter. The fullback has yet to log a carry this season, and he's caught eight of 11 targets for 76 yards and two touchdowns over six contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Pineiro went without a field-goal try for the second time this season, and he hasn't made multiple field goals in a contest since Week 1. To make matters worse, the kicker missed an extra-point try for the second straight week, and he's now 21-for-25 on PATs over the first seven games this season. With the 49ers off next week, Pineiro's next chance to be more involved will come in Week 9 against the Raiders.

With the 49ers' receiving corps down all of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle), Watkins saw an expanded role and made good use of the opportunity. All three of Watkins' catches went for first downs, and he finished third on the team in receiving yards and targets while also tying for that slotting in receptions. The 2025 fourth-round pick's performance was encouraging, but he's likely to slide back down the depth chart since the wide-receiver room could be much healthier by the time San Francisco returns to action against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following the Week 8 bye.

Christian McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury in the opening period that eventually led to him missing the entire second quarter, affording Black expanded opportunity. The rookie made good use of the extra touches, averaging a career-high 5.3 yards per carry and recording his highest rushing yardage total since his Week 1 NFL debut. Black also rang up his first TD as a professional, a 30-yard breakaway run on the first play of the second quarter. However, the rookie made a key mistake when he lost a fumble with San Francisco nearing the red zone in the second quarter. McCaffrey did return to the game for the second half and now has the Week 8 bye to recover, so Black could be back to a more reduced role in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Kittle led the 49ers across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets on an afternoon in which the team was down Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), and in which Christian McCaffrey missed the entire second quarter due to a quadriceps injury. All three components of the veteran tight end's receiving line were also season-best figures, but Kittle's lost fumble at the Falcons' 19-yard line with 57 seconds remaining following a 22-yard catch snuffed out any hope of a comeback for the Niners. Despite the unsavory conclusion to Sunday's game, Kittle will remain a key target for Brock Purdy in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following a Week 8 bye.

Williams started Week 7 prep as a non-participant but gradually worked his way up to full participation in Friday's session. The defensive end has overcome his knee injury in time to suit up opposite Keion White for Sunday's game.

Cross was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury he suffered during the Seahawks' Week 7 win over the Chiefs. Josh Jones will likely start at left tackle in the absence of Cross, whose next chance to play is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Knight opened Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices before logging a full session Saturday, and he's done enough to fade an injury tag against Chicago. The third-year linebacker has seen an uptick in defensive snaps over his last two outings, and he's logged 16 tackles (nine solo) in that span.

A back issue limited Murphy's practice participation Friday, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday Night Football. The third-year defensive lineman has logged 24 tackles (12 solo), including 3.0 sacks, through seven regular-season games.

Jones injured his hamstring in Week 7 against the Chiefs, and that prevented him from practicing all week. Luckily for the Seahawks, their backfield is near full strength, given that neither Zach Charbonnet (knee) nor Jadarian Price (chest, IR) carry injury designations ahead of Monday's contest. Jones' next chance to play is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Lock's practice reps during Week 8 prep were limited by a lingering elbow injury on his throwing arm. He opened the season as the Seahawks' backup QB and started in Week 2 against the Cardinals, but it's possible that he operates as Seattle's emergency third quarterback for a second consecutive game. In that case, he would not be allowed to play Monday unless both Sam Darnold and Jalen Milroe were to leave the game.

Shaheed will miss his first game of the 2026 season due to a knee injury that he sustained during the Seahawks' Week 7 win over the Chiefs. Tory Horton and Velus Jones are the top candidates to operate as Seattle's returners on kickoffs and punts, and Horton and Cooper Kupp should see a bump in offensive snaps in Shaheed's absence. Shaheed's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

The Seahawks designated Price for return from IR on Thursday, and he proceeded to be limited in practice that day before logging a full session Friday. Now that he's been given clearance for his first game action since Week 3 due to a chest injury, the team still needs to activate him from IR by 4 p.m. ET on Monday in order for him to be available in Week 8. Fellow running back Zach Charbonnet (knee) also doesn't have a designation this week, so Seattle's backfield suddenly is crowded, with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani also in the mix.

Charbonnet has been officially cleared to make his 2026 regular-season debut, marking the end to his rehab from a torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained in mid-January during the Seahawks' playoff run. The Seahawks' backfield will be whole for the first time this season, seeing as both Charbonnet and Jadarian Price (chest) have been cleared to play Monday, with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani providing depth.

O'Toole was held out of Week 7 against the Chiefs due to a hamstring injury, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that he'll be available against the Bears on Monday. He has three tackles (one solo) and one fumble recovery across four regular-season games while contributing mostly on special teams.

Surratt has missed the Seahawks' last four games while nursing a calf injury, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that he'll return for Monday's game against the Bears. The sixth-year pro mostly played on special teams prior to his injury.

Thomas missed Seattle's past two games and opened this week with a limited practice session. However, his ability to return to full participation Friday suggests the linebacker should be able to return to game action Monday versus Chicago. Thomas has started each of the five games in which he's appeared this season and has 20 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, one interception and one forced fumble.

Williams was limited Thursday due to an Achilles issue, but it appears the problem was only minor, as the veteran defensive end upgraded to full participation Friday. As such, he doesn't seem to be at risk of missing the Monday night matchup. Williams has continued to play a key role along the Seahawks' defensive line, though he hasn't logged a sack since taking down the quarterback in each of his first three games of the campaign.

Emmanwori was dealing with a hip injury heading into the weekend, but he was able to suit up and logged every one of Seattle's defensive snaps. Though he logged a modest four stops, Emmanwori was part of a dominant defensive effort by Seattle. Overall, Emmanwori has registered 27 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and one defensed pass through six contests on the campaign.

Jones had a three-game streak of recording at least one sack snapped, but he remained highly productive. The veteran linebacker has now tallied exactly nine tackles in three straight games and has posted at least eight stops in each of his seven contests this season. Overall, Jones is tied for third in the NFL with 68 tackles through seven games.

All five of Holani's carries came in the first half, but he didn't record a rush over the final two quarters as Emanuel Wilson dominated the Seahawks backfield to finish with 100 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries. Holani has logged five carries in three of his last four games, but he'll likely be demoted to RB3 duties against the Bears in Week 8 if Zach Charbonnet (knee) is cleared play in that contest.

Kupp entered Sunday's contest on the heels of a 10-target performance against the Broncos in Week 6. However, the veteran wideout saw only two looks from Sam Darnold, with the veteran quarterback relying heavily on favorite target Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who finished with a 9-150-1 line on 12 targets. Kupp has logged three targets or fewer in five of seven regular-season games, though he could see a slight bump in opportunities if Rashid Shaheed (knee) is unable to play against the Bears in Week 8.

Horton's 31 offensive snaps were third most among Seahawks wide receivers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (53) and Cooper Kupp (45). 17 of Sam Darnold's 28 pass attempts went to Smith-Njigba (12) and tight end AJ Barner (five), with Horton and the rest of Seattle's pass catchers serving in complementary roles. The Seahawks offense revolves around Smith-Njigba, so most of Horton's work will come on special teams, although the latter could see an uptick in opportunities if Rashid Shaheed (knee) cannot play against the Bears in Week 8.

Myers was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game, converting a 25-yarder in the second quarter before later adding a 35-yard make in the second half. The kicker has now gone 14-for-15 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over the first seven games of the 2026 campaign.

Darnold threw a 28-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second quarter to give the Seahawks a 10-0 lead, but Darnold's end-zone interception from the 3-yard line in the final minute of the first half allowed the Chiefs to stay within striking distance. Seattle's dominant defense made sure Darnold's eighth interception in five starts since returning from a glute injury wouldn't prove too costly. He has matched that interception total with eight touchdown passes over that span. Darnold and the 4-3 Seahawks will play at home in prime time again Week 8, hosting the Bears on MNF.

The afternoon-long rainy conditions in Tampa Bay and the Falcons' defense's complete inability to slow down the Buccaneers' ground attack led to Mayfield barely putting in any work as a passer. In the process, the Bucs became the first team since 1974 to win a game without a single completion, and the bizarre circumstances left Mayfield's fantasy managers with a dead spot in their lineups. Mayfield will naturally be a lot busier when he travels to the Windy City to face the Bears' aggressive defense in a Week 9 road showdown next Sunday night.

The Bucs attempted three total passes in Sunday's rain-soaked conditions, and Baker Mayfield didn't complete any of the three. Instead, Tampa Bay ran the ball 56 times and coasted to an easy win on the backs of Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and the defense. Godwin will do battle with the Chicago secondary next Sunday, positioning the veteran wideout as a WR4 in fantasy. Emeka Egbuka (foot) could be back for that game after missing the past two contests.

On a bizarre afternoon when the Buccaneers became the first team since 1974 to win a game without a single completion, Gainwell and backfield mate Bucky Irving carried the offense on their shoulders. Gainwell logged two fewer carries and gained 30 less yards than Irving, but the former's totals were both career highs. Gainwell showed no signs of the hip injury that had plagued him during the practice week, and thanks to back-to-back contests with highly unusual game scripts, the change-of-pace back has rushed for 228 yards on 39 carries over that span. Nevertheless, Gainwell still projects to serve in a clear complementary role behind Irving most weeks.

The Buccaneers became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass, so Irving was somewhat of a one-man wrecking crew as far as the offense was concerned. The talented running back's yardage total was a career-high figure, and the performance was the third of over 100 yards for Irving already this season. The third-year back added his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a four-yard run to close out the scoring with 3:47 remaining, and Irving is now up to 728 rushing yards and 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Bears next Sunday night.

Initially listed as questionable, Diaby has since been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's divisional meeting with Atlanta. As a result, David Walker will presumably absorb most of Diaby's snaps the rest of the way.

Goedeke earned the questionable tag for Week 8 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to return from a one-game absence due to a calf injury. He'll reclaim his starting spot at right tackle while Benjamin Chukwuma reverts to a depth role.
Barton picked up an illness over the weekend, but the third-year center has been cleared to play Sunday.

Johnson found a way to make an impact in Week 7 against the Panthers, Egbuka's first absence, despite the returning Baker Mayfield putting the ball up only 11 times for 64 passing yards. Johnson brought in both targets for 33 yards and a touchdown, and he also gained 14 yards on a rush attempt. In the process, the second-year wideout logged a season-high 41 snaps and outshined rookie Ted Hurst, who logged 35 snaps and failed to reel in his only target. While the depth chart reflects Hurst as ahead of Johnson, the latter may once again be the bigger beneficiary of Egbuka's absence against an Atlanta defense that's allowed the third-most receptions (96) to wide receivers this season.

Trotter opened the week as a non-participant Wednesday due to an illness, but he now appears to be good to go ahead of Week 8. The linebacker has recorded double-digit stops in back-to-back weeks, registering 22 total tackles (eight solo) and two passes defensed in those contests.

Hayes underwent a minor procedure on his knee after getting hurt in the preseason, and there's currently no timetable for his return following the setback. Once healthy, the 27-year-old should contribute on special teams.

Winfield has been sidelined for the Buccaneers' last three games while nursing a rib injury. He showed enough progression in his recovery to log a full practice Wednesday, which puts him on track to play against the Falcons on Sunday. Winfield should reclaim his starting role at safety, so Ifeatu Melifonwu figures to revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

Smith finished second on Tampa Bay in tackles, but his contributions extended well beyond that. He blocked a Ryan Fitzgerald extra-point attempt early in the second quarter and intercepted Bryce Young in the third. The pickoff was Smith's first of the season, giving him at least one interception in each of his first three NFL campaigns.

With Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) inactive, Hurst was expected to take on an expanded offensive role, but it was actually Tez Johnson who saw the bigger bump in playing time. Johnson played 41 snaps to Hurst's 35 and ran one more route (12) than the rookie wide receiver. The Bucs clobbered the Panthers, and Baker Mayfield was forced to drop back to pass just 11 times on the afternoon.

Daniels entered Sunday's contest late in the fourth quarter with Tampa Bay in full command of the contest, ultimately recording minus-3 rushing yards while kneeling on back-to-back plays to end the game. With Mayfield back in action, Daniels now will have to wait for his next chance to command the Buccaneers offense.

Otton went without a reception for the first time this season, and he has now combined to reel in one of three targets for four yards over the last two weeks. Tampa Bay leaned on the run in the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield, and Mayfield completed seven of 11 passes for just 64 yards in the victory. Otton figures to have much better days ahead as his quarterback gets back up to speed, and the tight end's first shot at getting back on track will come Week 8 against Atlanta.

Tucker was able to see an increase in touches for a third straight week, and as a result, he recorded a season-high 52 rushing yards. The running back's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he broke loose for a 46-yard rushing touchdown. Bucky Irving (24) and Kenny Gainwell (14) still had more carries than Tucker in Week 7, and he'll remain third in the pecking order at running back ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup with Atlanta.

McLaughlin was able to make multiple field goals for the second straight week and fifth time this season. The kicker converted a chip-shot 22-yard attempt in the second quarter before later adding a 44-yarder in the third quarter. McLaughlin has been far more involved in contests during which quarterback Baker Mayfield has been active, and the kicker will have a chance to make it three games in a row with multiple field-goal makes when the team hosts Atlanta in Week 8.

McCollum opened the week as a DNP due to an illness, but he upgraded his practice participation over the next two days and has been cleared to play in Sunday's NFC South tilt. The fifth-year defensive back has 27 tackles (22 solo), seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery through six regular-season games.

Rozeboom will be forced to miss at least four games while recovering from a finger injury that he likely suffered in Week 6 against the Steelers. In his absence, SirVocea Dennis will stand to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker behind starters Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter.

Sills had his 21-day practice window opened by the team Oct. 12, and he was able to open this week with back-to-back full practices. The wide receiver has been on IR since late August while recovering from a hamstring injury, but he will now slot in as a depth option behind Emeka Egbuka (concussion) and Chris Godwin moving forward this season.

With Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Dike receiving the biggest playing-time boost on offense, as he ran 40 routes on Cam Ward's 46 dropbacks. Only Gunnar Helm produced more receiving yards than Dike in the Week 8 defeat, and only Wan'Dale Robinson (six) recorded more catches. With the Titans headed into their Week 9 bye, Tate figures to be back the following week versus Jacksonville. Perhaps Dike can earn more playing time at Elic Ayomanor's expense, and Calvin Ridley's name has been linked to trade speculation.

Helm led the team in targets while he was able to register a new career-high 76 receiving yards in the contest. The tight end has now reeled in eight passes over the last two weeks after he caught nine of 13 targets for 60 yards over the first six games of the 2026 campaign. Helm will have a tough test against the Jaguars in Week 10 after the team's bye week in Week 9.

Robinson didn't experience a significant change in role in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder), as this was the fourth consecutive game in which Robinson notched either six or seven targets. His 57 receiving yards tied a season high, and Robinson scored his third touchdown of the season on a 15-yard catch in the fourth quarter. The Titans took a seven-point lead with 3:46 remaining after a successful two-point conversion following Robinson's TD, but the Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown drive and eventually won in OT to drop the Titans to 1-7. Robinson and the Titans will be on bye in Week 9 before returning to action against the Jaguars in Week 10.

Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

Pollard rumbled for a 40-yard touchdown in the first quarter and added a one-yard rushing TD in the third quarter, giving him five rushing scores in the last two games. He scored only once in the first six games of the season, but Pollard's recent hot streak has him up to six touchdowns, surpassing his total of five from each of his previous two regular seasons in Tennessee. Pollard was also brought down in Tennessee's end zone for a safety to break a 21-21 tie in the final minute of the third quarter. The surging running back has rushed for 246 yards over the past two games but could have a tough time maintaining his momentum after the Titans' Week 9 bye, as he'll return to action in a daunting Week 10 matchup against Jacksonville's league-best run defense.
With Skoronski sidelined, Garrett Dellinger is now in the game at left guard.
Latham sustained the injury in the fourth quarter. James Hudson has taken over at left guard in Latham's absence.
Williams has mostly worked on special teams this season, but his absence means the Titans will have less depth at linebacker for the rest of Sunday's contest.
The injury was severe enough for Harris to be carted off the field and into the locker room. Alontae Taylor will see more work in the secondary in Harris' absence.

Jones popped up on Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a knee injury, which is severe enough for him to not suit up Sunday. He's only worked on special teams across two regular-season appearances, but his absence means the Titans will also have less depth in the secondary. His next chance to play is Week 10 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 15.

The sixth-year tight end will be a healthy scratch for a third consecutive game and the sixth time this season. The Titans are on a bye for Week 9, so his next opportunity to suit up is Week 10 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 15. That said, Granson is unlikely to see the field unless there is an absence ahead of him on the tight end depth chart.

Franklin-Myers drew the questionable tag after ending Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices, and the veteran defensive lineman has been cleared by medical staff to suit up Sunday. He has 14 tackles (six solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through seven regular-season games, but he'll be tasked with a larger role on the defensive line in the absence of Jeffery Simmons, the latter of whom was traded to the Bears on Thursday.
